source.title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems

accepted.question_text: How can the BBGKY hierarchy for a time-dependent many-fermion system be truncated by reconstructing the next-higher reduced density matrix as a practical functional of lower-order reduced density matrices, especially by approximating the three-body reduced density matrix Γ(3) in terms of the one-body reduced density matrix γ and the two-body reduced density matrix Γ, so that one- and two-body observables can be propagated without solving the full hierarchy?

evidence.quote: In order to make the BBGKY hierarchy practical, we must truncate it at some level, n, by reconstructing the Γ (n+1) as a functional of lower-order RDMs.
there is no practical method available to find the exact functional and we have to use different approximations.
To this end, we need to truncate Eq.(10) by approximating Γ (3) in terms of γ and Γ.

accepted.question_text: How can closure approximations for time-dependent one- and two-body reduced density matrices be designed so that the propagated density matrices remain positive semidefinite and also satisfy fermionic occupation constraints, meaning natural orbital occupation numbers stay between zero and one, while avoiding unphysical negative local densities or divergent densities during electron dynamics?

evidence.quote: all RDMs are positive-semidefinite which refers to the fact that all eigenvalues of RDMs are always equal to or greater than zero.
in the case of fermionic particles, the Pauli exclusion principle enforces natural orbital occupation numbers to be less than or equal to one [23]. Thus, they have to remain between zero and one.

We conclude that, a possible way to make progress in the application of the BBGKY hierarchy is to make sure that positive-semidefiniteness of the density matrices and the fermionic constraints on the occupation numbers is built into the equations.

accepted.question_text: Why can sophisticated truncation approximations for the coupled BBGKY equations, including approximations motivated by Green's-function expansions, fail to obey fundamental physical constraints and lead to divergence of reduced-density-matrix dynamics even when the total particle number and total energy are conserved?
accepted.context_brief: Mechanism of divergence under conserved global quantities

evidence.quote: Such catastrophic behaviors of these coupled equations pose a valid question that why even highly advanced approximations based on the Green’s function expansion not only fail to follow fundamental physical principles, but also lead to divergence, even though the total energy and number of particles are conserved.
These tests show that the divergence problem is independent of the initial state and has to do with the nature of the approximated equations.

accepted.question_text: Can a variational or related time-propagation method impose positive semidefiniteness on the three-body reduced density matrix Γ(3), and on the resulting one- and two-body reduced density matrices γ and Γ, despite the fact that approximate truncation can break the trace relations connecting these density matrices?

evidence.quote: It is not easy to impose positive-semidefiniteness on Γ (3) and even if it has such property, since its trace relation with γ and Γ is broken this does not lead to the positive-semidefiniteness of γ and Γ.
However, we are exploring variational approaches to impose this constraint during the time evolution, namely preventing the system not to be positive-semidefiniteness.

accepted.question_text: How should the residual three-body correlation term Δ(3) in the cluster or cumulant expansion of the three-body reduced density matrix be approximated, beyond the three-body collision-integral-free, three-body noninteracting, and Wang-Cassing-style truncations, to obtain a more reliable BBGKY closure?

evidence.quote: For Γ (3) accordingly, we use a noninteracting particle form and add anti-symmetrized products of γ with the correlation function ∆ (2) – that partly describe the 3-body correlation – plus a remainder, ∆ (3)
Now, if we want to go beyond these approximations, ∆ (3) in Eq.(26) must be approximated.
there exist some approximations [33–35] – for instance, by using the connection between RDMs and the Green’s functions [33] – but we are not going to deal with them in this paper.

accepted.question_text: Do the instability, density-divergence, and fermionic-constraint-violation phenomena observed for BBGKY truncations in a finite Hubbard model persist in small molecules and more complex correlated-electron systems, and how can the proposed partial remedies be validated in those settings?
accepted.context_brief: Extension beyond the Hubbard-model test case

evidence.quote: although here we illustrate only the performance of all the approximations for the Hubbard model, our preliminary results for small molecules also exhibit very similar issues (work in progress [36]).

We propose some partial solutions of such problem and point the main paths for future work in order to make this approach applicable for the description of the correlated electron dynamics in complex systems.

accepted.question_text: What relationship between BBGKY reduced-density-matrix equations and approximate wave functions can be used to build time-dependent truncations whose natural orbital occupation numbers remain physical, as happens in time-dependent Hartree-Fock where a corresponding wave function exists?
accepted.context_brief: BBGKY closures tied to approximate wave functions

evidence.quote: For example in the case of the time-dependent Hartree-Fock, there exists always a wave function corresponding to the first equation of the hierarchy and therefore the natural orbital occupation numbers can never be unphysical.
This suggests a further study of the BBGKY equations in relation to (approximate) wave functions.

accepted.question_text: How can the BBGKY reduced-density-matrix approach be developed in linear response theory for optical spectra, where nonlinearities in the time-dependent hierarchy are removed by construction and may therefore avoid some of the divergence mechanisms seen in nonlinear propagation?

evidence.quote: Further progress can be made in linear response theory since in the linear response regime the nonlinearities are, by definition, removed and the BBGKY approach can be investigated further for the study of optical spectra.
Work along these lines is in progress.

accepted.question_text: How can time-dependent density-functional or reduced-density-matrix approximations incorporate nonlocality, memory dependence, time-dependent phases in functional terms, and energy conservation, instead of relying on adiabatic ground-state extensions that can produce pathologies such as time-independent occupation numbers?
accepted.context_brief: Nonadiabatic and energy-conserving TD functional approximations

evidence.quote: lack of proper exchange-correlation (xc) functionals for time-dependent systems hamper its applicability.

Most of the time-dependent approximations that are used so far, are adiabatic extensions of DFT approximations that disregards the non-locality and memory dependence of the time-dependent xc potential.

Ignoring this fact by using fixed signs may cause problems such as time-independent occupation numbers [20]. Furthermore, majority of these approximations do not necessarily conserve total energy of a system.

accepted.question_text: Is it possible to make propagation based only on the second BBGKY equation for the two-body reduced density matrix into a generally reliable approach, given that approximate closures can produce large total-energy fluctuations and can still diverge even when compatibility between the first and second hierarchy equations is no longer the immediate issue?
accepted.context_brief: Reliability of propagating only the second BBGKY equation

evidence.quote: Figure 4 shows that the energy fluctuations in time are relatively large for all the approximations, which puts a question mark over the quality of this approach in general.
the divergence in 3b-NIA or WC approximations has surfaced again and in fact, even the divergence time has not been improved in any of them.
we can confidently claim that the incompatibility is not the only cause of diverging behavior of the equations, and the role of positive-semidefiniteness should also be taken into account.
